parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain why the boiling point of $\text{SiO}_2$ is much higher than the boiling point of $\text{SO}_3$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is an amphoteric oxide.

Explain what is meant by the term *amphoteric*. Use chemical equations to illustrate your answer.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: State what you would observe when a small sample of $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ is placed in water.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Selenium is a Group 16 element which shows similar chemical reactions to sulfur.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Selenium reacts with fluorine to form $\text{SeF}_6$ molecules.

Predict the shape of a molecule of $\text{SeF}_6$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The most stable oxide of selenium is $\text{SeO}_2$.

Gaseous $\text{SeO}_2$ reacts to form a solid polymer, as shown. In the reaction one $\text{Se=O}$ is replaced by two $\text{Se-O}$ to form a polymer.

{{figure:visual_auto_01.png}}

Use these data to calculate the bond enthalpy, in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, of $\text{Se-O}$.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
$\text{SeO}_2$ shows similar chemical reactions to $\text{SO}_2$.

Suggest an equation to show the reaction of $\text{SeO}_2$ with aqueous sodium hydroxide, $\text{NaOH}$.
